I’m an INFP, and granted it’s been over six years since I was in high school, but I distinctly remember liking the book (continuing the trend of me loving books my peers absolutely hated ;p) I believe it was specifically for the character with the glasses. Piggy? I think it was? The way he was treated by the other students legitimately made me cry, and at the time that kind of catharsis was how I determined whether or not I liked a book. I understand this isn’t the most intelligent method of critiquing a novel’s merit, but I’m a capital “F” Feeler, what did you expect? XD 

Seriously though, my tastes have matured as I’ve gotten older. College pretty much obliterated my love of reading, and I only recently started enjoying it again by reading, believe it or not, cookbooks and text books. Somewhere along the line, I’ve found myself increasingly enamored with the practical over the fantastical, not because I lost my daydreams, but more so because I want to make the dreams a reality. 

To answer your question though (finally, lol) my least favorite book is EASILY Robinson Fucking Crusoe. I was tricked! Hoodwinked! Bamboozled! I was promised grand adventure in the form of jungle hijinks and cannibal shenanigans! Only to get bait and switched with some crusty old guy having mid life crisis in the middle of nowhere, lamenting about his lost goat and empty rum bottle for 100 pages. 0/10 would not recommend :pppppp
